transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
Russia fired ballistic missiles at Ukraine overnight,
hours after trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi
involving U.S. mediators wrapped up
with no major breakthroughs reached to end years of war.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley says President Trump's envoys
are to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin today in Moscow.
Head U.S. negotiator and President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner
told the media they had seen some openings and opportunities.
Skeptical Ukrainian negotiators were instructed to approach the talks
with an open mind if only to avoid annoying President Trump.
Ukrainians do not believe the Kremlin will miss the opportunity
to pummel Ukraine's severely weakened energy infrastructure
in this fifth winter of the war.
Analysts say Trump is looking for a foreign policy win
after his midterm drubbing,
but Putin has not backed off any of his maximalist demands,
such as Kiev handing over territory Russia has been unable to conquer.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kiev.
More than a week after the midterm elections,
Mississippi's Senate race has been called.
Democrat Scott Colombe defeated Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith.
Here's NPR's Elena Moore.
This race ultimately came down to just a few thousand votes,
taking over a week to call as election officials counted outstanding ballots.
It's a historic Democratic upset and a major blow to Republicans.
Even in a year where Democrats had momentum,
the Mississippi Senate race was not expected to be a toss-up heading into election day.
It's long been a ruby red state.
Just two years ago, President Trump carried Mississippi by double digits.
Now Colombe will be the first Democrat to represent the state in the Senate in more than 40 years.
He'll also be Mississippi's first black U.S. Senator since Reconstruction.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
Alaska's Senate race has yet to be called.
Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan by nearly 4,000 votes.
In New York, at least two people have been killed in the collapse of a three-story building in Brooklyn.
More than a dozen others have been injured, including children, as Steve Kestenbaum reports.
After the dust settled, what was left standing in Brooklyn's Flatbush neighborhood
looked like it had been sliced open.
A staircase was exposed along with a bedroom and a closet filled with clothing still on hangers.
Fire Department Chief John Esposito said rescue workers had to be very careful
as they searched for survivors in the rubble.
This is an extremely dangerous operation for all of our people.
Buildings Department Commissioner Ahmed Tagani said the structure collapsed into a construction site next door.
The type of work they were conducting was excavation work on that job site.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kestenbaum in Brooklyn, New York.
Wall Street futures are on the downside this morning.
This is NPR News from Washington.
The American Cancer Society is changing its prostate screening guidelines,
as NPR's Yuki Naguchi reports, it's now recommending regular PSA blood test screenings for men.
The Cancer Society previously recommended patients talk to their doctors
and share decision-making about whether to screen for prostate cancer,
which will be diagnosed in roughly 333,000 Americans this year.
Now, based on new data, it recommends PSA tests every other year for men between 50 and 69,
and annual screenings starting at age 45 for those at high risk,
like black men and people with strong family history.
One concern was that prostate cancer, which can be harmless in many men,
was being overtreated, causing more harm than good.
To prevent that, the Cancer Society is also recommending MRI
and additional blood tests before getting a biopsy.
Yuki Naguchi, NPR News.
Russian players are once again being banned from the upcoming World Junior Ice Hockey Championships in Canada.
The Secretary of Sport in Ottawa cites the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine.
The games are set to begin December 26 in Alberta for players under the age of 20.
Russian hockey players have been banned from the competition since 2022 because of the war.
Sotheby says a diamond-covered Romanov sapphire bracelet has sold at auction in Geneva
for nearly $5 million.
The winning bid was far higher than the auction house expected.
Sotheby says it went to a private collector.
It was once owned by Russia's imperial family.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: Russia fires ballistic missiles at Ukraine after inconclusive Abu Dhabi peace talks with U.S. mediators
Mississippi Senate race called: Democrat Scott Colombe defeats Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith
Alaska Senate race uncalled as Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican Dan Sullivan by about 4,000 votes
Brooklyn three-story building collapse kills at least two, injures more than a dozen including children
American Cancer Society now recommends regular PSA prostate screenings for men, with changes by age and risk
Canada bans Russian players from World Junior Ice Hockey Championships over ongoing war in Ukraine
Romanov sapphire bracelet sells at Geneva auction for nearly $5 million to private collector
